text: A yield farm adds a second income layer on top of an LP token: stake it into a rewards contract and the protocol emits its own token on top of the trading fees you're already earning.

Farm APY is annual reward value in dollars divided by total value locked. Two million dollars a year in rewards against ten million TVL is a 20 percent APY -- but that number is only as real as the reward token's price holding up.

The virtuous loop: emit rewards, attract LPs, deepen liquidity, generate more fee revenue. It breaks when farmers are only there for the reward -- they sell it immediately, the price falls, and they move to the next farm. That's mercenary capital.

Durable designs vest reward claims instead of paying out instantly, taper emissions on a schedule, and route a real-yield component from actual trading fees so some return survives even if the reward token's price falls to zero.

Trading fees are real revenue; emissions are a bet on the reward token's price. Next up: vaults and auto-compounding -- what happens when a strategy harvests and reinvests those rewards for you automatically.
